newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 90-day T-bill rate at 11.679 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 90-day T-bill rate at 11.679 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' bellwether 90-day Treasury bill rate rose to an average of 11.679 percent from 11.509 percent during the Monday regular weekly auction, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The other maturities also moved up in the light of the jitters caused by news that Philippine President Fidel Ramos underwent surgery for a cholesterol block in a major artery, dealers said.
The average 181-day T-bill rate jumped to 11.931 percent from 11.795 a week ago; and the 363-day T-bill soared to 12.455 percent from 12.199.
"People were bidding at the rates they were comfortable," a foreign bank dealer said.
Traders said banks currently want to stay liquid instead of investing in government securities due to the uncertainties caused by Ramos' health.
Investor cautiousness was reflected in the small amount of tenders received at the auction, which totaled 4.810 billion pesos, dealers said.
Only 3.325 billion pesos were accepted, short of the targeted sales of 3.5 billion pesos because of the high bids in the auction.
The 90-day T-bill rate garnered the most number of bids at 1.990 billion pesos, of which 1.0 billion pesos worth were awarded.
The 181-day bills, which had sales of 1.0 billion pesos, attracted 1.495 billion pesos worth of tenders.
And the 363-day bill had 1.325 billion pesos worth of tenders, which were all accepted.
